risks.risk: Malicious MCP servers, skills, plugins, or dependencies enter through the agent supply chain
controls: digest-verified catalog (tampered payload dropped at load; mismatch refused at install)
schema guard: depth/nodes/bytes/cycle bounds + object-root requirement
description size cap (payload-bomb descriptions rejected at discovery)
url policy: deny-by-default private/loopback/link-local — also enforced for HOOK targets (creation + dispatch re-check)
deny-by-default grants, terminal admin-only revoke, cross-tenant no-oracle (404)
custom-tool wrappers narrow arguments; revoked servers fail closed (SERVER_DISABLED)
team policy deny-wins enforced at calls, grant creation, and wrapper+source tools
shared service never imports extension code (SDK local-hook boundary)
S3: every connector intake is signature-verified on the raw body before parsing (real Slack/Sentry schemes; documented adapter schemes for Teams/Jira/alerts)
S3: tenant mapping fail-closed (403 TENANT_UNKNOWN, no existence oracle); per-tenant rate limit
S3: secret patterns redacted from incident text before it reaches a goal or any log line
S3: connectors can only PROPOSE plans (single-method gate client; no approve/run route exists on the service)
risks.remaining: No publisher signing/provenance beyond bundled digests; no external audit of curated payloads; comment-intake text (Jira/Linear bodies) could still embed injection strings — mitigated only by the human-approval gate on plans (untrusted-banner) this session; live SDK-to-S5 confinement chain remains for S5 evidence.
